analysis: The method levelToString(int level) converts an integer level constant into its corresponding string representation. It uses a switch statement with cases for four known constants: DANGLING, HIERARCHY, SIGNATURES, BODIES. If the level matches any of these, the method returns the string. The default case throws a RuntimeException with the message 'unknown resolving level'. This design indicates that the method expects only these four specific integer values. Any other integer is considered an invalid input, likely due to a programming error in the caller. Instead, it acts as a fail-fast mechanism to alert developers of a bug. The exception is intended to propagate up the call stack, possibly caught by a general exception handler or causing the program to terminate.
